title: What certificates, induction and drills do crew on Australian domestic commercial vessels need?
description: Marine Order 505 certificates of competency and Marine Order 504 induction, drill and first aid rules for domestic commercial vessels, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: On Australian domestic commercial vessels, the Australian Maritime Safety Authority applies two Marine Orders under the national law. Marine Order 505 (2022) sets 14 kinds of certificate of competency, each needing a minimum age of 16, a current HLTAID011 first aid certificate and medical fitness. Marine Order 504 (2024), in force since June 1, 2025, requires owners to give master and crew safety training, induction and emergency training before duties begin, run risk-based drills, and keep records for 5 years.
keyTakeaways: Marine Order 505 (Certificates of competency, national law) 2022 commenced on January 1, 2023; the current compilation applies from June 1, 2025.

First issue of any certificate of competency requires age 16 or over, sufficient English, Schedule 3 eligibility and sea service, a Certificate of Medical Fitness Domestic Seafarers and a current HLTAID011 first aid certificate.

Reissue of the senior certificates (Master under 45 m, Master under 100 m, Marine Engine Driver Grade 1, Engineer Class 3) needs 120 days of qualifying sea service in the previous 5 years or an approved alternative.
Schedule 1, clause 9 of Marine Order 504 requires safety training, induction and emergency procedures training for master and crew as soon as practicable after joining and before commencing duties.
Emergency drill frequency is set by each vessel's risk assessment, and induction, training and drill records must be kept for 5 years.
jurisdiction: Australia (Commonwealth national system for domestic commercial vessels)
regulator: Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), as National Regulator under the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012
appliesTo: Owners of domestic commercial vessels in Classes 1, 2 and 3 (Class 4 hire and drive vessels have separate Schedule 2 rules)
Masters, deck crew and engineers who need a certificate of competency for their duties
Shore staff engaged in key vessel operations, such as berthing
Registered training organizations approved by AMSA to conduct final assessments

sections.heading: Which rules set crew competence on domestic commercial vessels?

blocks.text: Two Marine Orders made under the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012 (the national law). [Marine Order 505 (Certificates of competency, national law) 2022](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2022L00423/latest/text) states that its purpose is "to provide for certificates of competency and set out standards for the qualifications of the crew and masters on domestic commercial vessels". It was registered on March 30, 2022, commenced on January 1, 2023, and was last amended from June 1, 2025.

[Marine Order 504 (Certificates of operation, national law) 2024](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2024L01458/latest/text) commenced on June 1, 2025 and repealed the 2018 version. Its Schedule 1 sets the safety management system requirements, including crewing, induction, drills, first aid and records. AMSA's [safety management systems page](https://www.amsa.gov.au/vessels-operators/domestic-commercial-vessels/safety-management-systems) confirms that the new SMS requirements took effect on June 1, 2025 for all domestic commercial vessels.

Seagoing ships on international voyages are certified under the Navigation Act 2012 and STCW instead; that regime is covered in [STCW seafarer training requirements](/regulations/stcw-seafarer-training-requirements).

sections.heading: What kinds of certificate of competency exist?

blocks.text: Section 8 of Marine Order 505 lists 14 kinds, all carrying the suffix NC (national certificate). A person must hold the certificate listed in Schedule 1 for any duty or function that Schedule 1 attaches to it, unless an exception applies.

items: **Deck and general:** General Purpose Hand; Coxswain Grade 3, Grade 2 and Grade 1; Sailing Master Coastal and Offshore.
**Master:** Master (Inland waters); Master under 24 m; Master under 45 m; Master under 100 m.
**Engineering:** Marine Engine Driver Grade 3, Grade 2 and Grade 1; Engineer Class 3.

blocks.text: Exceptions include holding a corresponding seafarer certificate under Schedule 2 or a certificate of recognition, working under a temporary crewing permit issued under section 16 of Marine Order 504, and limited Coxswain Grade 3 duties under section 7(5) by a person who meets the age, English, medical, first aid and eligibility criteria and keeps evidence of eligibility on board. A person with color deficient vision relying on that exception may only perform the duties in daylight.

sections.heading: What are the criteria to obtain and renew a certificate?

blocks.text: For first issue, section 9(1) requires the applicant to be at least 16, to be familiar enough with English to fully understand directions and documents for the duties, to meet the Schedule 3 eligibility and qualifying sea service requirements, and to hold a current Certificate of Medical Fitness Domestic Seafarers and a current first aid certificate equivalent to at least HLTAID011 Provide first aid.

For reissue, section 9(3) always requires a current HLTAID011 first aid certificate. For a Master under 45 m, Master under 100 m, Marine Engine Driver Grade 1 or Engineer Class 3, the applicant also needs a current medical certificate and at least 120 days of qualifying sea service in the previous 5 years in duties to which the certificate applies. For other certificates, a declaration of medical fitness in the approved form is enough.

Section 10(2) lists alternatives where the 120 days cannot be met: a final assessment approved by AMSA, 60 days of qualifying sea service in the 6 months before applying, 120 days in a seasonal fishery over 5 years for seasonal fishers, other industry experience approved by AMSA, or an AMSA approved task book. If a holder applies for reissue before expiry, section 7(3) lets them keep working for 90 days after expiry while they continue to meet the certificate's conditions.

blocks.title: Service before the certificate arrives
blocks.text: For seven entry and mid-level certificates, including General Purpose Hand, Coxswain Grade 1 and 2, Master under 24 m and Marine Engine Driver Grade 2 and 3, a person may start the duties on the day an approved final assessor signs the declaration, for up to 60 days or until AMSA decides the application (sections 22 and 23). The person must show the declaration to the owner, master or a marine safety inspector on request.

sections.heading: What induction, training and drills must owners provide?

blocks.text: Schedule 1, clause 9 of Marine Order 504, "Vessel induction, familiarisation, drills and training", requires the owner to ensure that master and crew, as soon as practicable after joining the vessel and before commencing duties, receive three things:

items: Safety training that familiarizes the person with safety matters about their presence and duties on board.
Induction in and familiarization with key vessel operations, to establish, maintain and verify the person's competence and capacity to safely carry out assigned duties.

Training in emergency procedures, to establish, maintain and verify the person's ability to respond rapidly and effectively and follow the emergency plan, covering the emergency plan's procedures and use of the vessel's life-saving equipment.

blocks.text: Emergency drills must be conducted at a frequency determined by the vessel's risk assessment and must test procedures and confirm the competence of master and crew to respond. The same training must be given to anyone else engaged in key vessel operations, with the example of an onshore staff member involved in berthing. The master, or a crew member the master considers has the appropriate skills and knowledge, must give the training. A note to the clause says induction and training should be repeated when key vessel operations or emergency procedures change.

Clause 9 is a certificate of competency's companion, not its substitute: a fully certified master joining a new vessel still needs that vessel's induction. The guide on [building a safety induction](/guides/how-to-build-a-safety-induction) covers how to structure one so it verifies competence rather than just recording attendance.

sections.heading: What other crew requirements does Marine Order 504 set?

items: **First aid (clause 10).** At least one person with a current first aid certificate equivalent to at least HLTAID011 must be available at all times, and a person qualified to operate the radio, either the master or deck watchkeeper, must be on board. The [first aid training requirements in Australia](/regulations/first-aid-training-requirements-australia) page covers HLTAID011 in workplace settings.
**Task allocation (clause 11(4)).** Each task in a key vessel operation procedure must be assigned to crew with the skills and knowledge to perform it.

**Passenger inductions (clause 11(5)(f)).** Vessels carrying passengers need a procedure for giving each passenger a safety induction on operational and emergency procedures, including lifejacket wearing, as soon as practicable after boarding.

**Crewing and rest (clauses 6 to 8).** Minimum crewing tables apply by vessel length, and crewing may not be set at the minimum unless master and crew can have at least 10 hours of rest in each 24 hour period.
**Crew list (clause 15).** An up to date crew list kept on board must show the certificates each crew member holds, including certificates of competency.

blocks.text: Operators running several vessels often keep these rows in one [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) with a vessel column, because the certificate is personal but the induction and drill evidence is vessel-specific.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry separates the personal layer (certificate of competency, first aid, medical fitness, sea service) from the vessel layer (induction, key vessel operations and drills) and links both to the Marine Order clause that requires them. An owner can then see, for any vessel and crew member, what is current, what is due and what the record must contain.

faqs.q: How often must emergency drills be held on an Australian domestic commercial vessel?
faqs.a: Marine Order 504 does not fix an interval. Schedule 1, clause 9(4) requires emergency drills at a frequency determined by the vessel's risk assessment, and the drills must test procedures and confirm the competence of master and crew. Records must be kept for 5 years.

faqs.q: What first aid qualification do domestic vessel crew need?
faqs.a: A current first aid certificate equivalent to at least HLTAID011 Provide first aid. Marine Order 505 requires it for first issue and every reissue of a certificate of competency, and Marine Order 504 requires at least one person with it to be available on board at all times.

faqs.q: Can I keep working if my certificate of competency expires while my renewal is processed?
faqs.a: Yes, for up to 90 days after expiry, if you applied for reissue before the certificate expired, the certificate was not revoked or suspended, and you continue to comply with its conditions. This is set out in section 7(3) of Marine Order 505.

faqs.q: Does a new crew member with a valid certificate still need an induction?
faqs.a: Yes. Schedule 1, clause 9 of Marine Order 504 requires safety training, induction in key vessel operations and emergency procedures training as soon as practicable after joining and before commencing duties, regardless of the certificates the person holds.
